description: Composite figure of six panels: five secondary-electron SEM micrographs plus one XRD pattern with offset baselines. (a₁) is an M1-HR SEM image (5 µm scale bar) with yellow arrows marking polygonal α-ferrite grains and lath-type α′+γ (martensite + austenite) regions; (a₂) is the dashed-box magnified view (3 µm scale bar) annotated α and α′+γ. (b₁–b₃) are M2-HR SEM images at 50 µm, 5 µm and 500 nm scale bars annotated α, δ (δ-ferrite) and α′+γ; the 500 nm panel resolves a fine lath/lamellar α′+γ morphology alongside blocky δ/α-ferrite. (c) plots XRD intensity (a.u.) versus 2θ = 40–110° for M1-HR (black) and M2-HR (red, vertically offset), with reflections labelled α 110, α 200, α 211, α 220 and γ 111, γ 200, and printed fγ values of 5.1 % and 5.7 %. The SEM panels identify ferrite (α, plus δ-ferrite in M2), austenite and a martensitic-austenitic α′+γ constituent; the XRD patterns confirm ferrite/martensite plus only a small austenite fraction in both samples.

subfigures.description: Secondary-electron SEM micrograph of the M1-HR sample, 5 µm scale bar. Yellow arrows point to polygonal α-ferrite and to lath-type α′+γ regions; a dashed rectangle marks the area magnified in (a₂).
Higher-magnification view (3 µm scale bar) of the dashed box in (a₁), showing more clearly separated α (ferrite) and α′+γ (martensitic-austenitic) constituents.
SEM micrograph of the M2-HR sample, 50 µm scale bar, with the widest field of view. Annotations α, δ and α′+γ with yellow arrows; a dashed rectangle marks the area magnified in (b₂).
Intermediate-magnification SEM micrograph (5 µm scale bar) of M2-HR showing δ-ferrite, α-ferrite and α′+γ laths; a dashed rectangle marks the region magnified in (b₃).
High-magnification SEM micrograph of M2-HR at 500 nm scale bar showing fine α′+γ lath/lamellar morphology between coarser α/δ-ferrite regions.

XRD patterns of M1-HR (black) and M2-HR (red), the red curve vertically offset; x-axis 2θ (°) from 40 to 110, y-axis Intensity (a.u.). Reflections labelled α 110, α 200, α 211, α 220, γ 111, γ 200; printed fγ values 5.1 % and 5.7 %.

observations.observation: Panels (a₁) and (a₂) are SEM micrographs of the M1-HR sample with 5 µm and 3 µm scale bars; (a₂) is the magnified dashed-box region of (a₁).
In (a₁) yellow arrows label polygonal α-ferrite grains and lath-type α′+γ (martensitic-austenitic) regions; (a₂) repeats the α and α′+γ annotation at higher magnification.
Panels (b₁), (b₂) and (b₃) are SEM micrographs of the M2-HR sample with 50 µm, 5 µm and 500 nm scale bars respectively, forming a successive zoom sequence linked by dashed rectangles.
Panel (b₁) carries three distinct annotations — α, δ (δ-ferrite) and α′+γ — whereas (a₁)/(a₂) of M1-HR carry only α and α′+γ, so δ-ferrite is labelled only in the M2-HR sample.

Panel (c) is an XRD plot with x-axis '2θ (°)' spanning 40 to 110 and y-axis 'Intensity (a.u.)'; the legend reads M1-HR (black) and M2-HR (red), the red M2-HR pattern drawn vertically offset above the black M1-HR pattern.
Peaks in (c) are labelled with α 110, α 200, α 211, α 220 (ferrite/martensite) and γ 111, γ 200 (austenite); the α 110 peak near 2θ = 45° is by far the most intense, and γ 111 lies just below 45°.

The text 'fγ = 5.1%' is printed at the level of the upper (red, M2-HR) trace and 'fγ = 5.7%' at the level of the lower (black, M1-HR) trace, which is opposite to the assignment in the citing text; the label-to-curve association is therefore ambiguous from the pixels alone.
The caption identifies (a₁-a₂) as the M1-HR sample, (b₁-b₃) as the M2-HR sample, and (c) as 'XRD plots for M1-HR and M2-HR samples'.
The caption states the SEM images are for showing the presence of different phases in the M1-HR and M2-HR samples.

The citing text states that SEM microstructures were taken in secondary electron (SE) mode and that the HR microstructures of both steels comprise multiple phases including ferrite, austenite and martensite.
The citing text attributes polygonal α-ferrite and lath-type martensitic-austenitic (α′+γ) phase to M1 steel, and δ-ferrite, α-ferrite and a very fine α′+γ phase to M2 steel.
The citing text states the XRD plots confirm ferrite/martensite and austenite in both samples and gives the austenite fraction as 5.1 % for M1 and 5.7 % for M2.
The citing text links the higher ferrite content, especially δ-ferrite, in M2 steel to the presence of Si, consistent with thermodynamic predictions in Fig. 1d, f.
The citing text notes that no numeric scale values other than the scale bars are printed on the SEM panels; quantitative phase fractions come from the XRD panel.

unreadable_items: panel (c): which printed fγ value (5.1 % or 5.7 %) belongs to M1-HR versus M2-HR cannot be resolved from label placement alone
panels (b₁) and (b₂): the small α, δ and α′+γ annotation text and the arrow targets are only partially readable at the supplied resolution
